about: How each surface of game/maps/surfaces.json looks. Render-only: not part of the world content hash, so no world-query result depends on it. Read by game/src/world/SurfaceLook.cs. Colours are photo-like sRGB albedos (reference notes terrain.md); a texture set is tinted so its mean matches. A surface without an entry gets default_set tinted to its surfaces.json albedo_srgb and the default vegetation.

straw.note: lodged dry straw over the soil, where cover.png G (straw) is set: belt floor, tilled residue streaks (T4, T3a)

litter.note: fallen leaves, where cover.png A (litter) is set: yards, bare belt floor (T6, T5)

meadow_sod.note: T1: mottled olive-khaki sod, green and straw-dry, with brighter yellow-green patches 2-5 m

dry_crust.note: T2: sun-baked loam crust with sparse dead tufts

belt_straw.note: T4: dark moist loam (the base colour here) under a lodged straw mat, standing stems with seed heads

belt_bare.note: T5: fine dry loam beaten bare, some leaves

tilled.note: T3a: dark loose loam; furrows are drawn from the physics ridges (azimuth, spacing, phase), straw residue from cover G

yard_litter.note: T6: compacted soil under fallen leaves

rubble.note: B5, T8: brick, concrete and plaster debris

weeds.note: T7: tall green-yellow leafy stalks and dry seed heads over ground shaded by them, so the soil reads much darker and greener than the meadow's khaki sod; the patches are the dry, opened-up gaps

burnt_field.note: T3b: black char and grey ash; stubble is charred stumps, litter is ash flakes
